name: mirage
text: Short answer: they were not profitable picks, they were break-even at best. I checked your 7 open parlays (stake $49 total) from the engine's ledger. At the time each was filled, our fair value was within 0.1-0.2 points of the price we quoted, so the expected profit is +$0.01 to +$0.04 each, about +$0.16 total on $49, with swings of roughly $10 either way. Per parlay (price vs fair win chance for the buyer): FSU -16.5 + FSU team total o88.5 .481/.479; Magic ML + Thunder -4.5 .499/.498 and again .503/.501 (the same two legs filled twice, which is what the new same-parlay guard now blocks); Chidekh ML + Herbert ML .446/.445; two NBA totals pairs at .265/.264 and .254/.253 ($25-27 of collateral each for a $9 stake); Romero Gormaz ML + Bronzetti ML .574/.573 (one leg already won). I can't give you a fair payout on fresh odds right now: the engine is off with a $0.05 wallet, so there are no live prices, and the ledger only keeps each parlay's fair as of the fill. The honest read is that margin was never the edge, as the data shows: a fill's value comes from selecting the right kinds of parlays (2 legs, price .15-.40, no leg over 80%), not from the +0.1 point margin. Several of these (heavy-favorite legs at 70-73% paired) are exactly the kind of leg the study says the buyers beat us on, and 4 of the 7 are same-leg or same-game duplicates. If you want, I'll re-price each open parlay against today's fresh leg odds next time the engine runs and post the gap here.
